```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(broom)
library(knitr)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
            theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.title.position = "plot"))
blue <- "#2a78d6"
orange <- "#eb6834"
grey <- "#8c8c8c"

# The warehouse is built by the Python/SQL pipeline: run `python run_pipeline.py` from the project root.
db_path <- file.path("..", "data", "warehouse.db")
if (!file.exists(db_path)) stop("data/warehouse.db not found. Run `python run_pipeline.py` from the project root first.")

con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), db_path)
adm <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM mart_admissions_detail")
ed <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT v.hospital_id, h.hospital_name, v.arrival_ts, v.arrival_hour, v.triage_level,
         v.wait_minutes, v.is_lwbs
  FROM fct_ed_visits v JOIN dim_hospital h USING (hospital_id)")
prm <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM ref_parameters")
dbDisconnect(con)

# Odds ratios with Wald 95% confidence intervals
tidy_or <- function(model) {
  tidy(model) |>
    mutate(conf.low = exp(estimate - 1.96 * std.error),
           conf.high = exp(estimate + 1.96 * std.error),
           estimate = exp(estimate))
}

pct <- function(x, accuracy = 0.1) percent(x, accuracy = accuracy)
fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3))

# Area under the ROC curve via the rank (Mann-Whitney) formula
auc <- function(y, p) {
  r <- rank(p)
  n1 <- sum(y == 1)
  n0 <- sum(y == 0)
  (sum(r[y == 1]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * n0)
}

hospital_levels <- c("Volcán Central", "Volcán Mixco", "Volcán Occidente", "Volcán Sur", "Volcán Norte")

idx <- adm |>
  filter(is_index_stay == 1, !is.na(age_at_admission)) |>
  mutate(
    age10 = age_at_admission / 10,
    payer_type = relevel(factor(payer_type), ref = "Private insurance"),
    clinical_category = relevel(factor(clinical_category), ref = "General surgery"),
    hospital = factor(hospital_name, levels = hospital_levels),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("F", "M"))
  )
```

## Summary

The SQL pipeline answers *what* happened. This report tests *whether the differences are real* and
*how big they are* once we control for patient mix. Data: `r comma(nrow(adm))` admissions and
`r comma(nrow(ed))` emergency department (ED) visits from five hospitals, `r prm$study_start`
to `r prm$study_end`.

```{r models}
#| include: false
# 1. Readmission risk factors
m_risk <- glm(is_readmitted_30d ~ age10 + charlson_index + payer_type + sex + clinical_category + hospital,
              data = idx, family = binomial())
or_risk <- tidy_or(m_risk) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")
or_of <- function(t) or_risk$estimate[or_risk$term == t]
auc_risk <- auc(idx$is_readmitted_30d, fitted(m_risk))

# 2. Program evaluation (difference-in-differences) on the four target conditions
tgt <- idx |>
  filter(is_program_target == 1) |>
  mutate(treated = as.integer(program_group == "Program hospitals"),
         post = as.integer(program_period == "Post"))
m_did <- glm(is_readmitted_30d ~ treated * post + age10 + charlson_index + icd10_code,
             data = tgt, family = binomial())
m_lpm <- lm(is_readmitted_30d ~ treated * post + age10 + charlson_index + icd10_code, data = tgt)
did_or <- tidy_or(m_did) |> filter(term == "treated:post")
did_pp <- tidy(m_lpm, conf.int = TRUE) |> filter(term == "treated:post")
naive <- tgt |> filter(treated == 1) |> group_by(post) |> summarise(rate = mean(is_readmitted_30d))
naive_pp <- diff(naive$rate)

# 3. ED: long waits and patients leaving without being seen
low <- ed |>
  filter(triage_level >= 3) |>
  mutate(hour_cell = substr(arrival_ts, 1, 13)) |>
  group_by(hospital_id, hour_cell) |>
  mutate(avg_wait_in_hour = mean(wait_minutes, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(is.finite(avg_wait_in_hour)) |>
  mutate(wait_30 = avg_wait_in_hour / 30, triage_level = factor(triage_level))
m_lwbs <- glm(is_lwbs ~ wait_30 + triage_level + hospital_id, data = low, family = binomial())
lwbs_or <- tidy_or(m_lwbs) |> filter(term == "wait_30")

# 4. Cost drivers
cost <- adm |>
  filter(!is.na(total_cost_gtq), !is.na(age_at_admission)) |>
  mutate(age10 = age_at_admission / 10,
         clinical_category = relevel(factor(clinical_category), ref = "General surgery"),
         hospital = factor(hospital_name, levels = hospital_levels))
m_cost <- lm(log(total_cost_gtq) ~ los_days + icu_days + age10 + charlson_index + clinical_category + hospital,
             data = cost)
cost_eff <- tidy(m_cost, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  mutate(pct_change = exp(estimate) - 1, lo = exp(conf.low) - 1, hi = exp(conf.high) - 1)
eff_of <- function(t) cost_eff$pct_change[cost_eff$term == t]
```

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Who gets readmitted? | Each extra comorbidity point raises the odds by `r pct(or_of("charlson_index") - 1)`, each decade of age by `r pct(or_of("age10") - 1)`, and self-pay patients have `r pct(or_of("payer_typeSelf-pay") - 1)` higher odds. The model's AUC is `r round(auc_risk, 2)`. |
| Did the transitional care program work? | Yes. Relative to comparison hospitals, readmissions for target conditions fell by **`r round(-100 * did_pp$estimate, 1)` percentage points** (95% CI `r round(-100 * did_pp$conf.high, 1)` to `r round(-100 * did_pp$conf.low, 1)`; odds ratio `r round(did_or$estimate, 2)`, p `r fmt_p(did_or$p.value)`). A naive before/after comparison would claim `r round(-100 * naive_pp, 1)` points. |
| Do long ED waits drive walk-outs? | Every extra 30 minutes of average wait raises the odds of leaving without being seen by `r pct(lwbs_or$estimate - 1)`. |
| What drives cost? | Each extra day in hospital adds `r pct(eff_of("los_days"))` to the cost of a stay and each ICU day another `r pct(eff_of("icu_days"))`. The model explains `r pct(summary(m_cost)$r.squared, 1)` of the variation in (log) cost. |

## 1. Who gets readmitted within 30 days?

Logistic regression on `r comma(nrow(idx))` index stays. Odds ratios above 1 mean higher risk,
holding the other factors constant. Reference groups: private insurance, female, general surgery,
Volcán Central.

```{r fig-risk}
#| fig-height: 6
or_risk |>
  mutate(term = gsub("payer_type|clinical_category|hospital", "", term),
         term = recode(term, age10 = "Age (per 10 years)", charlson_index = "Charlson index (per point)", sexM = "Male"),
         term = reorder(term, estimate)) |>
  ggplot(aes(estimate, term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = grey, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), width = 0.2, colour = blue, orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(colour = blue, size = 2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Diagnosis, comorbidities and payer drive readmission risk",
       x = "Odds ratio (log scale, 95% CI)", y = NULL)
```

```{r tbl-risk}
or_risk |>
  transmute(Term = term, `Odds ratio` = round(estimate, 2),
            `95% CI` = paste0(round(conf.low, 2), "-", round(conf.high, 2)), `p-value` = fmt_p(p.value)) |>
  kable()
```

**Reading it.** Medical admissions (cardiology, oncology, pulmonology) carry several times the odds of a
surgical stay. After adjusting for case mix, Volcán Norte still has `r pct(or_of("hospitalVolcán Norte") - 1)`
higher odds than Volcán Central, which matches the risk-adjusted ranking in the SQL marts. Sex has no
measurable effect (p `r fmt_p(or_risk$p.value[or_risk$term == "sexM"])`).

## 2. Did the transitional care program reduce readmissions?

From `r prm$program_start`, Volcán Central and Volcán Occidente call patients 24-72 hours after
discharge for heart failure, AMI, pneumonia and COPD. The other three hospitals are the comparison group.

```{r fig-did}
tgt |>
  mutate(d = as.Date(discharge_date),
         quarter = as.Date(paste0(format(d, "%Y-"), sprintf("%02d", (as.integer(format(d, "%m")) - 1) %/% 3 * 3 + 1), "-01"))) |>
  group_by(program_group, quarter) |>
  summarise(rate = mean(is_readmitted_30d), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(quarter, rate, colour = program_group)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.Date(prm$program_start), colour = grey, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Comparison hospitals" = grey, "Program hospitals" = blue)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Readmissions for target conditions dropped only where the program started",
       x = NULL, y = "30-day readmission rate", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r tbl-did}
tgt |>
  group_by(Group = program_group, Period = program_period) |>
  summarise(`Index stays` = n(), `Readmission rate` = pct(mean(is_readmitted_30d)), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(Group, desc(Period)) |>
  kable()
```

**Difference-in-differences.** The interaction `treated × post` estimates the program effect after removing
the network-wide trend and adjusting for age, comorbidities and diagnosis:

- Linear probability model: **`r round(100 * did_pp$estimate, 1)` percentage points**
  (95% CI `r round(100 * did_pp$conf.low, 1)` to `r round(100 * did_pp$conf.high, 1)`).
- Logistic model: odds ratio **`r round(did_or$estimate, 2)`** (95% CI `r round(did_or$conf.low, 2)`-`r round(did_or$conf.high, 2)`, p `r fmt_p(did_or$p.value)`).

```{r pretrend}
pre <- tgt |>
  filter(post == 0) |>
  mutate(d = as.Date(discharge_date),
         q = (as.integer(format(d, "%Y")) - 2023) * 4 + (as.integer(format(d, "%m")) - 1) %/% 3)
m_pre <- glm(is_readmitted_30d ~ treated * q + age10 + charlson_index + icd10_code, data = pre, family = binomial())
pre_p <- tidy(m_pre) |> filter(term == "treated:q") |> pull(p.value)
```

**Is the comparison fair?** The key assumption is that both groups were on parallel trends before the
program. In the pre-period the difference in quarterly trends is not significant
(p = `r round(pre_p, 2)`), so the assumption is reasonable.

**Caveats.** With only two program hospitals the result depends on them being typical; standard errors
are not clustered by hospital (five clusters are too few for reliable clustering). Comparing patients who
answered the call with those who did not would be biased (reachable patients are healthier), which is
why the evaluation compares hospitals, not individuals.

## 3. Emergency department: waiting times and walk-outs

```{r fig-ed-hour}
ed |>
  filter(!is.na(wait_minutes), triage_level %in% 3:5) |>
  group_by(hospital_name, arrival_hour) |>
  summarise(median_wait = median(wait_minutes), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(hospital_name = factor(hospital_name, levels = hospital_levels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(arrival_hour, median_wait, colour = hospital_name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 3)) +
  labs(title = "Waits peak late morning and early evening; Mixco and Norte are slowest all day",
       subtitle = "Median door-to-provider time, triage levels 3-5",
       x = "Hour of arrival", y = "Minutes", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r ed-tests}
urgent <- ed |> filter(!is.na(wait_minutes), triage_level == 3)
kw <- kruskal.test(wait_minutes ~ factor(hospital_name), data = urgent)
pw <- pairwise.wilcox.test(urgent$wait_minutes, urgent$hospital_name, p.adjust.method = "holm")
```

**Are the hospital differences real?** For urgent (level 3) patients a Kruskal-Wallis test rejects equal
waiting times across hospitals (H = `r comma(round(kw$statistic))`, p `r fmt_p(kw$p.value)`). Pairwise
Wilcoxon tests with Holm correction:

```{r tbl-pw}
as.data.frame(pw$p.value) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), "", fmt_p(.x)))) |>
  kable()
```

**Walk-outs.** Patients (triage 3-5) are grouped by the average wait of others seen in the same hospital
and hour. Controlling for triage level and hospital, each extra 30 minutes raises the odds of leaving
without being seen by **`r pct(lwbs_or$estimate - 1)`**
(95% CI `r pct(lwbs_or$conf.low - 1)` to `r pct(lwbs_or$conf.high - 1)`).

```{r fig-lwbs}
low |>
  mutate(band = cut(avg_wait_in_hour, c(0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, Inf),
                    labels = c("<30", "30-60", "60-90", "90-120", "120-180", "180+"), right = FALSE)) |>
  group_by(band) |>
  summarise(lwbs = mean(is_lwbs), n = n()) |>
  ggplot(aes(band, lwbs)) +
  geom_col(fill = blue, width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(lwbs)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "The longer others are waiting, the more patients walk out",
       x = "Average wait in the same hour (minutes)", y = "Left without being seen")
```

## 4. What drives the cost of a hospital stay?

Linear regression on log(cost) for `r comma(nrow(cost))` billed stays, so each coefficient reads as a
percentage change in cost. R² = `r round(summary(m_cost)$r.squared, 3)`.

```{r tbl-cost}
cost_eff |>
  filter(term %in% c("los_days", "icu_days", "age10", "charlson_index") | grepl("^hospital", term)) |>
  transmute(Driver = recode(gsub("^hospital", "Hospital: ", term),
                            los_days = "Each extra day of stay", icu_days = "Each ICU day (on top of the stay)",
                            age10 = "Each decade of age", charlson_index = "Each Charlson point"),
            `Effect on cost` = pct(pct_change),
            `95% CI` = paste0(pct(lo), " to ", pct(hi)),
            `p-value` = fmt_p(p.value)) |>
  kable()
```

```{r fig-cost}
#| fig-height: 5.5
cost |>
  mutate(diagnosis = reorder(diagnosis, total_cost_gtq, median)) |>
  ggplot(aes(total_cost_gtq, diagnosis)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = blue, alpha = 0.25, colour = blue, outlier.alpha = 0.15, outlier.size = 0.6) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma(prefix = "Q")) +
  labs(title = "Surgical and cardiac stays cost the most per case",
       x = "Cost per stay (GTQ, log scale)", y = NULL)
```

**Reading it.** Once length of stay and ICU days are known, age and comorbidities add little to cost:
the cost of a stay is driven by **how long** the patient stays and **where** (ICU), plus the procedure.
Hospital differences reflect price levels (Volcán Central, in the capital, is the most expensive). That
makes length of stay the main operational lever for cost, and readmissions a direct cost: every avoided
readmission saves a full additional stay.

## Recommendations

1. **Extend the transitional care program** to the three comparison hospitals, starting with Volcán Norte
   (highest risk-adjusted readmissions), and add sepsis and diabetes, the next-highest-risk conditions.
2. **Staff the ED to the arrival curve** at Volcán Mixco and Volcán Norte (late morning and evening peaks);
   cutting average waits by 30 minutes would lower walk-outs by roughly `r pct(1 - 1 / lwbs_or$estimate, 1)` in relative terms.
3. **Target self-pay patients at discharge** (medication access, follow-up appointment before leaving):
   they have the highest readmission odds and leave against medical advice most often.
